title: perf(canary): KV-aware hysteresis + enhanced auto-detection for rollout guards
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Improved performance canary auto-detection with KV-aware baselines and hysteresis to reduce false-positive regressions during cache warmup. Adds rollout guard logic to pause/rollback traffic shifts when sustained regressions are detected.
description:
Context: We continue to see flaky perf canary signals caused by KV cache warmup and short-lived tail-latency spikes during traffic shifts. These false positives lead to unnecessary rollbacks or halted rollouts. This PR introduces a KV-aware auto-detection strategy and hysteresis to the performance canary detector and extends rollout guards to (1) understand cache warmup windows, (2) require sustained signal before pausing or rolling back traffic, and (3) use weighted baselines to avoid overreacting to cold-start noise.

What this PR does: - Adds a KV-aware baseline estimator that separates requests that hit the KV cache vs. miss, and computes independent baselines and thresholds for each path. - Implements hysteresis in the detector: a two-stage detection window (short-term detection + confirmation window) before triggering a guard action. - Introduces traffic-hold semantics in rollout guards: when a confirmed regression is detected the canary will hold at the current traffic percentage and either automatically roll back after a configurable timeout or abort the rollout depending on severity. - Adds configurable bootstrap periods per-model/variant to avoid treating initial cold-start latency as regressions. - Updates perf-canary UI + API to show KV-hit/miss breakdown, hysteresis state, and recommended mitigation actions. - Adds unit tests and a focused perf test harness scenario to validate behavior under simulated KV warmup loads.

Why: This reduces noisy alerts and unnecessary rollbacks for models with warm KV caches (e.g. long-context streaming workloads) and makes rollouts more stable across heterogeneous backends.

Linear/Related: ENG-1423 (perf canary false positives), ENG-1589 (rollout guard features), ENG-1610 (kv-cache telemetry). Support ticket SUP-4821 surfaced a customer incident where a dedicated rollout was repeatedly halted due to transient p95 shifts.

Implementation notes and tradeoffs: - Baselines are maintained per-variant and per-KV-state; this increases memory for metrics (configurable TTL). - Hysteresis windows are conservative by default (short detect 3 min, confirm 10 min) and are configurable per deployment. - We chose weighted baselines (exponential decay) to adapt more quickly to traffic changes while dampening single-sample spikes. - Does not change core runtime scheduling; this is a detection/guarding layer to be incrementally enabled per-customer.

Testing done: - Unit tests for detector logic and hysteresis transitions. - Synthetic perf canary scenarios with KV warmup where baseline converges correctly and no false alert is raised. - End-to-end staging rollout with canary traffic that demonstrates hold-and-rollback behavior on sustained regressions.

Migration/ops notes: - Default rollout behavior stays unchanged for existing customers; feature can be toggled via perf-canary config flag. - Recommend enabling on Dedicated and Private first (observability required).

Checklist: - [x] Detector algorithm + hysteresis implementation - [x] KV-hit/miss baseline estimator - [x] Rollout guard traffic-hold + rollback timeout - [x] API/console updates (metrics + state) - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Perf test harness scenario - [x] Docs/Linear links updated

If merged, follow-up work: - ENG-1702: expose per-tenant tuning defaults - ENG-1715: auto-calibrate hysteresis windows based on workload class

review_comments: Arjun: The KV-hit/miss split makes a lot of sense. Two questions: how do you handle cross-variant cache effects (same GPU pool, different variant)? Can we make the baseline TTL tenant-scoped?

Maya (author): Good point — baseline keys include variant + tenant id; cross-variant effects are possible and we added a config to optionally aggregate at GPU-pool level (off by default). Baseline TTL is configurable per-tenant in perf_canary_defaults.yaml.
Sofia: Can we reduce the default confirm_window for small models? 10 min might be too long for low-traffic services.
Maya: Added per-variant bootstrap/confirm overrides; defaults stay conservative but operators can tune. Also added a short-path for low-traffic classes in the detector config.
Liam: CI showed a flaky integration test on first run — I re-ran and it passed. Suggest adding a retry wrapper for the synthetic harness to reduce flakiness.
Maya: Added retry in test harness and an explanatory comment.
